abstract: Using three unique datasets from North Dakota, I study the effects of the fracking boom on post-graduation outcomes and high school graduation rates of North Dakota high schools using a difference-in-differences design. The oil boom sharply increased wages and employment in core oil counties. Adolescents in core oil counties responded by decreasing 4-year college enrolment rates 23%, with no reduction in 2-year college enrolment. Notably, college enrolment rates also decreased for women. Results immune to in-migration bias indicate that 4-year college enrolment decreased 16% in core oil counties. No evidence suggests that the boom impacted high school graduation rates of men or women.
authors: Paul Niekamp Miller College of Business
title: Bakken out of education? Effects of the North Dakota oil boom on educational attainment
title_zh: 北达科他州石油繁荣对教育程度的影响：巴肯地区是否被教育遗忘？

abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology is reshaping the global economic and social structure, and its wide application empowers the sustainable development of enterprises. Using micro data from Chinese listed enterprises and adopting a two-way fixed effe ct model, this paper examine the impacts of AI on enterprise ESG performance. The research indicates that AI promotes the overall enterprise ESG performance, and this conclusion still holds after the robustness tests, endogenous tests and the ESG sub-dimensional regression test. In non-state-owned enterprises, enterprises with low financing constraints, non-labour-intensive enterprises and high-tech enterprises, the promotional effect of AI on enterprise ESG performance is more obvious. The mechanism tests reveal that the effects of AI on enterprise ESG performance primarily arise through its influence on green technology innovation, strategic deviance, and analyst concern. Consequently, economic agents and policy makers should emphasize the significance of AI application to improve enterprises ESG performance.
